t: Program Call-Graph Analyzer: a plain-language overview
title: Program Call-Graph Analyzer: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Program Call-Graph Analyzer does and why archives need it. A program call-graph analyzer reads code and draws the map of who calls whom: main calls parse, parse calls validate, and so on. The map reveals dead code nobody calls, recursive loops, and the exact paths to any function. A codebase becomes a navigable graph.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Program Call-Graph Analyzer works
title: How the Program Call-Graph Analyzer works
description: Overview: what the Program Call-Graph Analyzer does and why archives need it. Real analyzers extract call sites from ASTs (every Call node, its function name, its location), resolve names to definitions through symbol tables, and build a directed graph of caller-to-callee edges. Reachability analysis from entry points finds dead code; cycle detection finds recursion; and path queries answer 'how can execution reach this function?' Dynamic dispatch (virtual methods, callbacks) is handled with class-hierarchy or points-to approximations, marked as approximate edges.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Program Call-Graph Analyzer works: the deep tour
title: How the Program Call-Graph Analyzer works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Program Call-Graph Analyzer does and why archives need it. Real analyzers extract call sites from ASTs (every Call node, its function name, its location), resolve names to definitions through symbol tables, and build a directed graph of caller-to-callee edges. Reachability analysis from entry points finds dead code; cycle detection finds recursion; and path queries answer 'how can execution reach this function?' Dynamic dispatch (virtual methods, callbacks) is handled with class-hierarchy or points-to approximations, marked as approximate edges. Advanced analyzers build context-sensitive graphs distinguishing separate calls to the same function, integrate with type information for precise dispatch resolution, and scale to millions of lines with incremental updates. Quality is measured by edge precision/recall against dynamic traces. The limits are reflection, eval, and plugin architectures where calls are genuinely unknowable statically — those become unknown-target edges rather than false precision, because a wrong call graph misleads every analysis built on it.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.
